chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Salih ibn Abi Hammad narrated to me. He said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said:
When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wishes goodness for a people, He appoints for them a merciful ruler, and assigns to him a just vizier.

key_terms.رعية: Ra'iyya - subjects, populace, community under governance
key_terms.سلطان: Sultan - ruler, sovereign authority, political leader
key_terms.وزير: Wazir - vizier, minister, chief advisor to the ruler

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Sadiq say about just governance and merciful rulers in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), in a teaching reported through al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, explains that divine favor toward a community manifests through righteous leadership. This was shared in a gathering context during al-Saduq's assembly in 368 AH, reflecting classical Islamic political ethics where just governance is understood as a sign of God's care for a nation.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa al-Daqqaq (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Salih b. Abi Hammad narrated to me. He said: Muhammad b. Isma`il b. Baziq narrated to me from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Mufaddal b. `Umar. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) said:
If Allah wishes goodness to an outcast, He gives her a merciful ruler, and appoints a just vizier for him.
